newsitem.title: PERU: Mothers snubbed anew in Peru crisis mediating bid.
newsitem.headline: Mothers snubbed anew in Peru crisis mediating bid.

text.p: Ignored by President Alberto Fujimori and barred from meeting with hostages or jailed rebels, one of Latin America's best known human rights groups failed again on Monday to play a role in ending Peru's hostage crisis.
Peruvian authorities "don't know us too well. They don't know what we do," said Hebe de Bonafini, president of Argentina's Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo. "I think they are a little confused."

A delegation of the Mothers, famous for their struggle against Argentina's military dictatorship in the 1970s, arrived in Lima last week, invited by Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels to mediate in the crisis.
A band of about 15 heavily armed MRTA rebels stormed the Japanese ambassador's Lima residence on Dec. 17 and continue to hold hostage 72 mostly middle-aged men.

Sporting their trademark white scarves over their white hair, the Mothers trooped on Monday to Government Palace for the second time in three days only to be told Fujimori, who was travelling in Peru's eastern jungle, would not receive them.
Bonafini told local television she hoped to have better luck on Tuesday, when news reports say the delegation also plans to return to Buenos Aires.
Earlier on Monday, the group of two Mothers and their lawyer were rebuffed at a Lima women's prison and barred by armed police from reaching the residence to meet with the hostages.
The main demand of the rebels is freedom for about 400 jailed comrades who they say are being held in inhumane conditions.

Bonafini told reporters the group was concerned about conditions in Peru's prisons for both common criminals and convicted guerrillas. She said the hostage crisis was a "delicate situation" but added her group has "great hopes that it will end well. That's why we're here."
